quests.question: The committee's decision to implement the new policies ___ widely contested.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the committee's decision' (singular) - all other words are modifiers.
quests.explanation: The subject is 'the committee's decision', which is singular. The long modifier ('to implement the new policies') does not change agreement. 'The decision was widely contested'.

quests.question: The committee's decisions to implement the new policies ___ widely contested.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the committee's decisions' (plural) - all other words are modifiers.
quests.explanation: The subject is 'the committee's decisions', which is plural. 'The decisions were widely contested' - even with a long modifier, the subject controls the verb.

quests.question: The extent to which digital technology ___ transformed education is debated.
quests.hint: Inside the 'to which' clause, 'digital technology' is singular - uncountable.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded clause, the subject is 'digital technology', which is singular and uncountable. 'Digital technology has transformed education' - singular verb.

quests.question: The extent to which digital technologies ___ transformed education is debated.
quests.hint: Inside the 'to which' clause, 'digital technologies' is plural.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded clause, the subject is 'digital technologies', which is plural. 'Digital technologies have transformed education' - plural verb.

quests.question: The extent of the changes required ___ significant.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the extent' (singular) - 'of the changes required' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The extent' is the singular subject; 'of the changes required' is a prepositional modifier. 'The extent is significant'.

quests.question: The scale of the reforms that ___ proposed last year is now clear.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'that' refers to 'the reforms' (plural).
quests.explanation: Inside the relative clause 'that were proposed last year', 'that' refers to 'the reforms', which is plural. The verb inside the clause is 'were'.

quests.question: What the long-term consequences of this policy ___ is difficult to predict.
quests.hint: Inside the embedded clause, 'the long-term consequences' is plural.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded clause 'what the long-term consequences of this policy are', the subject is 'the long-term consequences', which is plural. The verb inside is 'are'.

quests.question: What the long-term consequence of this policy ___ is difficult to predict.
quests.hint: Inside the embedded clause, 'the long-term consequence' is singular.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded clause, the subject is 'the long-term consequence', which is singular. The verb inside is 'is'. Note: changing 'consequences' to 'consequence' changes the agreement.

quests.question: The hypothesis that the researchers ___ testing proved to be correct.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'the researchers' is plural.
quests.explanation: Inside the relative clause 'that the researchers were testing', the subject is 'the researchers', which is plural. The verb inside the clause is 'were'.

quests.question: All that ___ needed now is patience and persistence.
quests.hint: 'All that' functioning as a singular noun clause takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'All that is needed' uses 'all that' as a singular noun clause. It means 'the only thing that is needed', which is singular.

quests.question: All those who ___ interested should submit an application by Friday.
quests.hint: 'All those who' refers to multiple people - plural verb inside the clause.
quests.explanation: 'All those who are interested' uses 'those' to refer to multiple people. The verb inside the relative clause is 'are' because 'those' is plural.

quests.question: The committee, which ___ made up of twelve members, meets quarterly.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'the committee' (singular collective).
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'the committee', which is a singular collective noun. The verb inside the relative clause is 'is made up'.

quests.question: The number of cases reported each year ___ fallen significantly.
quests.hint: 'The number of' is always singular - one total count is being described.
quests.explanation: 'The number of' is always singular. 'The number of cases has fallen significantly' - not 'have'. One number is being discussed.

quests.question: A significant number of cases ___ reported each year despite the vaccine.
quests.hint: 'A significant number of' means 'many' - plural verb with a plural noun.
quests.explanation: 'A significant number of cases' means 'many cases'. Like 'a number of', 'a significant number of' takes a plural verb when followed by a countable plural noun.

quests.question: Whether the new approach ___ effective remains to be seen.
quests.hint: Inside the 'whether' clause, 'the new approach' is singular.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded 'whether' clause, the subject is 'the new approach', which is singular. 'Whether the new approach is effective' - singular verb inside the clause.

quests.question: The question of whether these methods ___ ethical continues to be debated.
quests.hint: Inside the 'whether' clause, 'these methods' is plural.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded clause, the subject is 'these methods', which is plural. 'Whether these methods are ethical' - plural verb inside the embedded clause.

quests.question: The assumption that underlies these arguments ___ questionable.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the assumption' (singular) - the relative clause is descriptive.
quests.explanation: 'The assumption' is the singular subject; the relative clause 'that underlies these arguments' describes it. 'The assumption is questionable'.

quests.question: The assumptions that underlie these arguments ___ questionable.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the assumptions' (plural) - relative clause is descriptive.
quests.explanation: 'The assumptions' is the plural subject; 'that underlie these arguments' describes them. 'The assumptions are questionable'.

quests.question: The pace at which these industries ___ growing has surprised many economists.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'these industries' (plural).
quests.explanation: Inside the relative clause 'at which these industries are growing', 'which' refers to 'these industries', which is plural. The verb inside is 'are'.

quests.question: The pace at which this industry ___ growing has surprised many economists.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'this industry' (singular).
quests.explanation: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'this industry', which is singular. The verb inside the clause is 'is': 'at which this industry is growing'.

quests.question: The way in which these challenges ___ addressed will determine the outcome.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'these challenges' (plural).
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'these challenges', which is plural. The verb inside the relative clause is 'are': 'in which these challenges are addressed'.

quests.question: The way in which this challenge ___ addressed will determine the outcome.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'this challenge' (singular).
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'this challenge', which is singular. The verb inside is 'is': 'in which this challenge is addressed'.

quests.question: Five years ___ a long time to work in the same position without promotion.
quests.hint: A specific time period treated as one unit takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: When a period of time is treated as a single unit or amount, the verb is singular. 'Five years is a long time' - we see it as one duration.

quests.question: Millions of euros ___ spent on the project every year.
quests.hint: A large sum expressed as multiple units takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: Unlike 'fifty dollars is too much', large sums expressed as multiple units take plural verbs when the emphasis is on the individual units. 'Millions of euros are spent'.

quests.question: Ten minutes ___ all the time we have left to finish this.
quests.hint: A duration treated as a single unit of time takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: When 'ten minutes' is treated as a single block of time (not individual minutes), the verb is singular: 'ten minutes is all the time we have'.

quests.question: The ten minutes we spent waiting ___ not entirely wasted.
quests.hint: Here 'the ten minutes' refers to individual minutes in a sequence - plural.
quests.explanation: When 'the ten minutes' refers to the individual minutes that passed, rather than a single unit of time, the verb is plural: 'the ten minutes were not entirely wasted'.

quests.question: The criteria used to evaluate the proposals ___ clearly defined.
quests.hint: 'Criteria' is the plural of 'criterion' - always takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'Criteria' is the plural form of 'criterion'. It is always plural and always takes a plural verb: 'the criteria were clearly defined'.

quests.question: The criterion used to evaluate this proposal ___ clearly defined.
quests.hint: 'Criterion' is the singular form - it takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'Criterion' is the singular form of 'criteria'. When you refer to just one standard, the verb is singular: 'the criterion was clearly defined'.

quests.question: The phenomena observed during the experiment ___ remarkable.
quests.hint: 'Phenomena' is always plural - never singular.
quests.explanation: 'Phenomena' is the plural of 'phenomenon'. It is always plural and takes a plural verb: 'the phenomena were remarkable'.

quests.question: The phenomenon observed during the experiment ___ remarkable.
quests.hint: 'Phenomenon' is singular - it takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'Phenomenon' is the singular form of 'phenomena'. When referring to one occurrence, the verb is singular: 'the phenomenon was remarkable'.
